pill.desc: clear, colorless to pale brownish-yellow solution in a single-dose prefilled syringe

tell: An anti-IgE antibody with a boxed warning for anaphylaxis and an elimination half-life of 26 days in asthma.

clues.text: Average absolute bioavailability after subcutaneous injection is 62%. Clearance combines general protein-degradation routes, including the liver reticuloendothelial system, with target-mediated clearance.
Has a molecular weight of about 149 kilodaltons. Sterile and preservative-free, and the vial form is a lyophilized powder.
A BLA product in 75, 150 and 300 mg prefilled syringes and autoinjectors, and 150 mg vials, dosed every 2 or 4 weeks.

Boxed warning for anaphylaxis, which can occur after the first dose or beyond 1 year. Contraindicated after severe hypersensitivity to it or its ingredients; nasopharyngitis and headache are common in children.
Moderate to severe persistent asthma with allergen sensitivity, chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps, food allergy, and chronic spontaneous urticaria.
Binds IgE and inhibits its binding to the high-affinity IgE receptor on mast cells, basophils and dendritic cells, causing receptor down-regulation.
The generic name begins with O and has ten letters.
